newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Sterling in fine fettle on all fronts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Sterling in fine fettle on all fronts.

text.p: The pound hit a 52-month high against the yen on Wednesday, boosted by aggressive buying by Japanese investors attracted to sterling's comparatively high-yield, traders said.

Sterling also gained on the mark against a backdrop of fresh European economic monetary union (EMU) jitters after news that a compromise plan that would allow Italy to join EMU after 1999 was being considered.
The break through the psychologically important 200 yen level invigorated the pound on all fronts. It rose over three pfennigs against the mark and was up over a cent against the dollar.
Market nerves after the monetary meeting between Finance Minister Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England (BOE) Eddie George also pushed the pound higher, traders said.
Comments made by Clarke on television after the meeting were interpreted that he was implying a change in rates had been agreed. However, the Treasury said nothing should be read into those remarks.

The BOE offered help to the money market at established rates in afternoon operations. A rate change is still possible at the second round on Thursday morning, but a Reuters poll taken before the meeting showed 23 out of 24 expected no change in rates. A recent spate of soft economic data dampened hopes for a near-term interest rate rise.

But in the longer term, British rates are still expected to rise as the economy grows above trend. Sterling is bound to benefit as interest rate expectations elsewhere in Europe and in Japan are focused on easier credit rather than tigthening.

"The recent adjustment of rate expectations means that this is a non-issue for the pound, especially as EMU tensions and Samurai issues are supporting the currency," said Teis Knuthsen, economist at First Chicago in London.
The pound eroded the psychologically important 200 yen level to trade at its highest since October 1992 on follow-through buying after aggressive demand by Japanese investors overnight.

Sterling buying was also linked to the issue of dual-currency Samurai bonds, traders said. An apparent shift from Australian dollar assets into sterling-denominated investments was also driving sterling/yen gains overnight.
Mild profit-taking pushed sterling back from its high at 201.30 yen to 200.95 at 1500 GMT, up from 198.50 at the previous close here.
Chartists said the next big level on the charts is 203 yen, a 61.8 percent retracement of the pound's entire move from the 1992 high at 249.20 to the 1995 low at 128.33.
Sterling was 2.6671 marks, off an earlier high at 2.6920 but up from 2.6562 at the previous close here. Against the dollar, it was at $1.6309, up from $1.6211 at the close on Tuesday.
